stories.headline: Pujari blames BJD’s ‘failure’ for flood
stories.title: Pujari blames BJD’s ‘failure’ for flood
stories.summary: Odisha Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari dismisses BJD chief Naveen Patnaik’s "man-made flood" claims, attributing recent disaster impacts to long-standing governance failures and unprecedented rainfall during Cyclone Arnab.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Odisha Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari dismisses BJD chief Naveen Patnaik’s "man-made flood" claims, attributing recent disaster impacts to long-standing governance failures and unprecedented rainfall during Cyclone Arnab.

Bhubaneswar: Joining the ongoing debate over Biju Janata Dal president Naveen Patnaik’s description of the recent flood as man-made, Odisha minister Suresh Pujari on Thursday blamed the previous BJD government’s “failure” to implement mitigation measures during its 24-year rule for the disaster.
Pujari, the Revenue and Disaster Management Minister, also claimed that no loss of life was reported in three cyclones after the BJP came to power in the State two years ago.

However, according to officials, of the 11 deaths and six people reported missing following Cyclone Arnab, 10 people died in landslides in Ganjam and Kandhamala districts, while one man was swept away in floodwaters in Gajapati district.
Pujari said, “I have high regard for Naveen Babu, who was the chief minister for 24 years.

But do you have any answer on the loss of human lives in calamities during the BJD tenure?” The flood management by the Mohan Charan Majhi government is certainly the best in the recent past, as no human casualties were reported in Cyclone Arnab and the floods, except in landslides, he told reporters.
“As many as 9,866 people died in the 1999 Super Cyclone during the Congress period.
Seventy-two people lost their lives in Cyclone Titli, 45 in Cyclone Phailin, and 65 in Fani under the BJD tenure,” Pujari said.
He said the Majhi government has faced three cyclones—Dana, Mantha and Arnab—during its 28 months in office.
Pujari said there is no such scientific forecast or prediction of landslides in India.
“However, we are undertaking studies on such incidents to avoid human casualties in future,” he said.

Rejecting the Opposition’s allegations of a “man-made flood” in Ganjam, Pujari said the State government was prepared for a detailed debate on the matter in the Assembly, which commences on November 18.

stories.headline: Search operations launched across south Kashmir
stories.title: Search operations launched across south Kashmir
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 12: Security forces on Thursday launched and intensified search operations across south Kashmir in the wake of the terror attack on a CRPF checkpoint near Mir Bazar in Kulgam district, even as the joint cordon-and-search operation at the main site entered its second day with an expanded area under cordon. The primary operation, which was suspended overnight due to darkness, resumed at first light in the Nowpora Akhran area. Additional forces have been deployed, barricades strengthened and vehicle checks intensified along the Srinagar-Jammu National Highway and approach roads to seal escape routes. Armoured vehicles and Quick Reaction Teams remain in position as teams comb the forested and rural belts. GOC 15 Corps, Lieutenant General Balbir Singh, visited the spot to review the operations and take stock of the ground situation. Senior officers of the Army, CRPF, and J&K Police are supervising the search, which is being guided by human and technical intelligence inputs. Parallel search and area-domination efforts have been activated at multiple locations across south Kashmir as part of a coordinated response. The attack occurred around 2:15 pm on Wednesday when two heavily armed assailants emerged from a dense cluster of trees and opened fire on a CRPF naka of the 46th Battalion, deployed as a bridge guard roughly 1 to 2 km off the Srinagar-Jammu National Highway near Mir Bazar. Security personnel returned fire, but the attackers fled into the adjoining forested area. The injured personnel have been identified as Head Constable Somveer Singh (Madhya Pradesh), Constable RakeshDass (Assam) and Constable Santosh Chandru (West Bengal). Somveer Singh sustained a bullet injury to his arm and RakeshDass to his leg; both were reported stable. Chandru suffered gunshot wounds to the abdomen and spine and was initially critical. Two of the injured personnel have since been discharged from hospital after treatment. The critically injured jawan was airlifted to the 92 Base Hospital in Srinagar for advanced care. Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha visited the hospital to enquire about his condition and interacted with the treating doctors. Deputy Commissioner Anantnag Bilal Mohiuddin had earlier visited the injured at GMC Anantnag. This is the third terror-related incident reported in south Kashmir in recent months. Forces have maintained a tight vigil across the region while the expanded searches continue.

stories.headline: AIP reviews party expansion, expresses hope for early verdict on Er Rashid’s bail plea
stories.title: AIP reviews party expansion, expresses hope for early verdict on Er Rashid’s bail plea
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 12: The Awami Itihaad Party (AIP) Thursday convened an Executive Committee meeting in Srinagar under the chairmanship of Party Vice Chairman Advocate G N Shaheen. The meeting, as per a statement, was attended by General Secretary (Org) Prince Parveez General Secretary Nazir Ahmad Khan, Chief Spokesperson Inam Un Nabi, State Secretary Sheikh Ashiq, senior party leaders including MLA Langate Sheikh Khursheed, Peerzada Firdous Ahmad Baba, Mir Nazir Ahmad, Parvez Ahmad Bhat and Advocate Dawood Ahmad. The Executive Committee expressed concern over the continued incarceration of Party President and Member of Parliament Engineer Rashid. Taking note of the fact that the Delhi High Court has reserved its judgment on his regular bail application, the committee expressed hope that the verdict would be delivered at the earliest, paving the way for his release and enabling an elected Member of Parliament to resume his public responsibilities. The meeting also reviewed the ongoing membership drive across Jammu and Kashmir. Members expressed satisfaction over the encouraging public response and described the growing interest in joining the party as a positive indication of its expanding organisational reach. Detailed discussions were also held on strengthening the party organisation, reviewing existing party structures and improving coordination at different levels. Special emphasis was laid on expanding AIP’s organisational presence and building a stronger base across the Jammu Province. The Executive Committee reiterated its commitment to organisational consolidation, grassroots outreach and strengthening the party’s presence across all regions of Jammu and Kashmir.

stories.headline: Trump threatens Mexico with doubled tariffs as nearly 2,000 migrants head towards US border
stories.title: Trump threatens Mexico with doubled tariffs as nearly 2,000 migrants head towards US border
stories.summary: Nearly 2,000 migrants head to the US border as Trump warns of Mexico tariffs if the caravan advances, fueling immigration and policy tensions
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Nearly 2,000 migrants from Central and South America are heading towards the US southern border following the Democrats' gains in the midterm elections, with US President Donald Trump threatening to immediately double tariffs on Mexico if it fails to stop the caravan from reaching American territory.

In a post on Truth Social on Thursday (local time), Trump linked the formation of new migrant caravans to the Republicans' performance in the midterm elections, claiming that the movement was taking place following the party's electoral losses.
He said, "Here we go again!
With the perceived loss by the Republicans in the Midterms - I was not on the ballot- the invasion of our Country is taking place again.
Huge caravans are forming and beginning their illegal march through Mexico.
Many of the people in these Caravans are those that various countries don’t want - “Send them to America,” they say - But they will not be accepted!”
He warned, "Mexico must stop them now, and if they do not do so, the Tariffs on Mexico will be immediately doubled.
Mexico, the Governor of Texas, the very liberal new Governor of Texas, our great Border Patrol & ICE, have been so informed.
There will be no leniency!
Thank you for your attention to this matter."
Fox News reported that migrants travelling with the caravan expected the Democrats to welcome them and provide opportunities to build new lives in the United States.
One migrant told Fox News, "We are seeing it this way because we know that the Democrats are not going to let a point as big as the Latino vote be lost.

stories.headline: PM Modi, Rajnath Singh attend wedding reception of Dogra royal family scion in Delhi
stories.title: PM Modi, Rajnath Singh attend wedding reception of Dogra royal family scion in Delhi
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 12: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and several other prominent political leaders attended the wedding reception of Rajkumar Martand Singh, son of former J&K minister Vikramaditya Singh, and Rhea Badal, daughter of senior BJP leader Manpreet Singh Badal, in New Delhi. The reception brought together several top senior political leaders, members of former royal families, diplomats, industrialists and spiritual leaders. PM Modi congratulated the newly married couple and interacted with members of both families. Among those present were Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia, who is the groom’s maternal uncle, and Minister of State in the PMO Dr Jitendra Singh. Former Jammu and Kashmir Chief Ministers Farooq Abdullah and Ghulam Nabi Azad, former Chief Justice of India T S Thakur, Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini and Lok Sabha MP Anurag Thakur also attended the reception. US Ambassador to India and Special Envoy Sergio Gor, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister P K Mishra, Shiromani Akali Dal president Sukhbir Singh Badal and former Union Minister Harsimrat Kaur Badal were among the other prominent guests. Spiritual leader and head of Radha Soami Satsang Beas, Baba Gurinder Singh Dhillon, also blessed the couple. Members of former royal families of Gwalior, Jaipur, Jodhpur, Jaisalmer, Bastar and Patiala were among those attending the celebration. Martand Singh is the son of Vikramaditya Singh and Chitrangada Raje, elder sister of Jyotiraditya Scindia, and grandson of former Union Minister Dr Karan Singh. Rhea Badal is the daughter of Manpreet Singh Badal and Vinu Badal. Vikramaditya Singh and Chitrangada Raje thanked Prime Minister Modi and other dignitaries for attending the reception and blessing the newlyweds.

stories.headline: Centre sanctions new roads, infrastructure along China’s border
stories.title: Centre sanctions new roads, infrastructure along China’s border
stories.summary: The Indo-Tibetan Border Police sanctions the construction of 15 pedestrian suspension bridges and 18 log bridges in Arunachal Pradesh; CCS clears 26 new roads as part of ICBR-III
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Amid continuing face-offs with the Chinese Army along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh since late July, the Indo-Tibetan Border.
Police (ITBP) has sanctioned the construction of new border infrastructure in the northeastern State, a senior government official told.
The Hindu.
Earlier, in February, the Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) had cleared the third phase of the Indo-China Border Roads (ICBR-III) project.
Under the scheme, as many as 26 roads are to be constructed along the LAC in Arunachal Pradesh, another government official said.
The Union Government has not yet officially announced the ICBR-III project or publicly disclosed these details.
This is only the second time after the 2020 Galwan clashes in eastern Ladakh that a critical road infrastructure project has been sanctioned along the border with China.

The first phase of the ICBR was initiated in 2005 when it was decided that the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) would construct 27 priority roads with a total length of 608 km along the border with China.

The second phase of the ICBR, comprising 32 roads with a total length of 683 km, was approved on September 21, 2020, just months after 20 Indian soldiers were killed in violent clashes with the Chinese People’s Liberation Army in eastern Ladakh.

Since September, the ITBP has authorised the construction of 15 pedestrian suspension bridges and 18 log bridges in Upper Subansiri and Kurung Kumey districts, covering the areas bordering China in Arunachal Pradesh.
The project clearance came days after India hosted the 18th BRICS Summit from September 11 to 13 in New Delhi, which was attended by Chinese President Xi Jinping.

A government statement after the meeting said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi emphasised that peace and tranquillity in the border areas remains an essential basis for the continued development of bilateral relations.

stories.headline: 'Criminal Law Moves Fast Against Poor, But Not Influential': Madras High Court As Centre Sanctions Prosecution Of 2 IAS Officers
stories.title: 'Criminal Law Moves Fast Against Poor, But Not Influential': Madras High Court As Centre Sanctions Prosecution Of 2 IAS Officers
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Secretary to Government, Department of Personnel and Training, has informed the Madras High Court that the Central Government has accorded sanction to prosecute two IAS officers in connection with the tender irregularities scam.
When the matter came up for hearing, Justice Anand Venkatesh was informed that the Centre had accorded sanction to prosecute the two officers – KS Kandasamy and K Vijaya Karthikeyan.
The court was also informed that the investigating agency would be acting upon the sanction and take steps to conduct an investigation against the officers and file a final report.

Taking note of the sanction, the judge orally remarked that the present case was a classic example of how the criminal law worked in the country where the law moved fast against the poor but needed a push when the case related to influential people.
“Classic case of how criminal law works in this country.
See how much effort has been put in by so many people.
Things move fast for poor people.
But for influential people, we have to push and push, and ultimately we are here,” the court orally remarked.
The court was hearing a contempt petition filed by NGO Arappor Ayakkam against the delay in proceedings against former Minister SP Velumani and three IAS officers in a tender irregularities case.
SP Velumani is accused of abusing his official position while he was serving as the Minister for Municipal Administration.
It is alleged that he had extended large-scale favouritism while awarding tenders for road works in Chennai Corporation and Coimbatore Municipal Corporation to his relatives and his close associates.
Arappor Iyakkam, an NGO, made a complaint with the DVAC.
